grf.leading_hypothesis: The package-index mode-loss seam is dangerous only if a resolver treats ClayPackageIndex/v1 as semantically complete; the merged resolver avoids that specific failure by source-hash-bound reparse.
grf.strongest_counter_reality: Reparsing can preserve syntax intent yet still overclaim name-binding semantics if it assumes every plain use path denotes an exact module.
grf.discriminator: Compare the merged v1 exact-module rule with authorized corpus examples in which the final path component is an exported declaration rather than a module.
grf.observed_result: The corpus contains use frank.entity.Frank while the provider module is frank.entity and Frank is an entity declaration; therefore plain-use-as-exact-module is not justified.
grf.collapse: RETAIN the hash-bound reparse and deterministic provider identity mechanism; REJECT universal exact-module semantics for plain MODULE-mode uses; DEFER plain-use name binding until an explicit namespace contract exists.
